task: P1 Strict-safe mode — reject operations without proven safety
counting_rule: Only diagnostics containing a literal '[CPLUS-' token count as tagged C+ enforcement (docs/libc/AGENT1_COMPILER_GAPS.md §0). An untagged rejection is PARTIAL, not a strict-safe pass. A proven error (both modes reject) is distinct from an unverified operation (default warns / strict must reject).
definition_of_reject_without_proven_safe: Strict-safe mode must reject at compile time (non-zero exit from 'c+ check --strict' with a [CPLUS-...] diagnostic) any operation whose safety the compiler cannot prove from translation-unit facts: (1) raw pointer arithmetic/deref whose address is not proven within a live object's extent; (2) an allocation of foreign provenance (raw malloc) used with a checked stdlib API; (3) a bounded-wrapper dmax/smax that is not a proven upper bound or derived from tracked capacity metadata; (4) a raw FILE* operation not routed through the managed wrapper; (5) a void* to typed pointer cast whose type/extent is not justified by provenance; (6) an indirect call whose target is not a known direct callee or a provably in-range table entry. DEFAULT may warn; STRICT fails closed. Contract: ../c-plus-core/compiler/Driver/Driver.h:67-69 and AstSafetyCheck.cpp:2159-2161.

summary.conclusion: All six unverified operations are accepted identically by --strict and --default (rc=0, no [CPLUS- diagnostics, no warnings). This is the P1 capability gap. A positive control (non-literal printf format) shows strict does fail closed on a documented unverified op, so the flag is not a no-op.

raw_evidence_convention: For each case, exact stdout/stderr/exit are stored in <stem>.strict.stdout, <stem>.strict.stderr, <stem>.strict.rc and <stem>.default.stdout, <stem>.default.stderr, <stem>.default.rc in this directory. The strings below are verbatim copies of those files.

cases.operation: raw pointer arithmetic on a stdlib object (string_view::data() + 100 deref)
cases.delta: none: identical accept and output in both modes

cases.operation: unchecked raw malloc used with a stdlib API (cplus_memset_s on raw malloc block with unproven capacity)
cases.delta: none: identical accept and output in both modes

cases.operation: unproven capacity passed to a bounded wrapper (cplus_memcpy_s with caller-parameter dmax/smax)
cases.delta: none: identical accept and output in both modes

cases.operation: raw FILE* operation outside the file wrapper (fopen/fread/fclose with caller-supplied length)
cases.delta: none: identical accept and output in both modes

cases.operation: cast from void* to typed pointer (stdlib_alloc void* cast to int* and subscripted)
cases.delta: none: identical accept and output in both modes

cases.operation: function-pointer call with unproven target (table[volatile cmd]() indirect call)
cases.delta: none: identical accept and output in both modes
